349829.title: Lin, Liu and Lu's maximum distance energy conjecture for clique trees
349829.statement:
Let $G$ be a clique tree of order $n$ whose cliques are $K_{n_1},\ldots,K_{n_k}$. For a clique path $\mathbb{P}_{m_1,\ldots,m_k}$, let $\mathbb{P}_{m_1,\ldots,m_k}$ denote the graph obtained by replacing the edges of a path on $k+1$ vertices with cliques of orders $m_1,\ldots,m_k$, with consecutive cliques intersecting in one vertex and all other clique intersections empty. The distance energy of $G$ is $E_D(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n|\lambda_i(G)|$, where $\lambda_i(G)$ are the eigenvalues of its distance matrix. **Lin, Liu and Lu's conjecture.** Among all clique trees with cliques $K_{n_1},\ldots,K_{n_k}$, the graph attaining maximum distance energy is

$$
\mathbb{P}_{\left\lfloor \frac{n-k+3}{2}\right\rfloor,2,\ldots,2,\left\lceil \frac{n-k+3}{2}\right\rceil}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the extremal distance energy among clique trees with prescribed clique structure; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

349831.title: Hirschorn's conjecture on extremal cross-intersecting families
349831.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $N_{prod}(n,a,b,t)$ denote the maximum product of the sizes of two cross-$t$-intersecting families, one consisting of $a$-subsets of $[n]$ and the other of $b$-subsets of $[n]$. A pair of families is **cross-$t$-intersecting** when every member of the first intersects every member of the second in at least $t$ elements.

**Hirschorn's conjecture.** The quantity $N_{prod}(n,a,b,t)$ is attained on some pair of families of the form

$$
\mathcal F=\left\{F\in\binom{[n]}{a}:|F\cap[s]|\geq u\right\},\qquad \mathcal G=\left\{G\in\binom{[n]}{b}:|G\cap[s]|\geq v\right\},
$$

where $u,v,s\in[n]$ satisfy $u+v=s+t$.

This conjecture proposes that extremal cross-$t$-intersecting pairs always have a common initial-segment threshold structure. The supplied text does not state whether this all-parameter conjecture has been resolved; it therefore remains open in this record.

350025.title: Wang–Zhang's neighbor refinement of Spiro's conjecture
350025.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}_n$ be the set of ballot permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{O}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$ whose cycles all have odd length. For distinct letters $i,j\in[n]$, let $\mathcal{B}_n(i,j)$ consist of ballot permutations in which $i$ and $j$ are neighbors of $n$, and let $\mathcal{O}_n(i,j)$ consist of odd-order permutations in which $i$ and $j$ are cyclic neighbors of $n$. Write $\mathsf{des}(\pi)$ for descent number and define $\widetilde\mathsf{exc}(\pi)=\sum_C\min(\mathsf{casc}(C),\mathsf{cdes}(C))$ using cyclic ascent and descent numbers on the cycles of $\pi$. **Wang–Zhang's conjecture.** For any distinct letters $i\ne j$,

$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{B}_n(i,j)}t^{\mathsf{des}(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{O}_n(i,j)}t^{\widetilde\mathsf{exc}(\pi)}.
$$

This is a refinement of Spiro's conjecture obtained by tracking the two neighbors of the largest letter. The supplied text identifies it as a proposal of Wang and Zhang but gives no evidence that the full refinement has been resolved.

350721.title: Signed cycle-type restriction polynomiality conjecture
350721.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $k$ be a fixed positive integer with $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ elements. For $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, let $\operatorname{type}(\pi)$ be its cycle type, and let $\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)$ and $\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)$ denote its right-to-left-minimum-value and excedance-value multisets, respectively. Then **the polynomiality conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\min(\operatorname{type}(\pi))\geq k}}(-1)^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}\mathbf{x}_{\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)}\mathbf{y}_{\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)}
$$

is an element of $\mathbb{N}[x_1,\dotsc,x_n,y_1,\dotsc,y_n]$. This generalizes the derangement case by imposing a lower bound on the lengths of all cycles; the source provides no resolution or further evidence for the claim, so its status remains open.

350925.title: The core classification conjecture for right-angled Artin groups
350925.statement:
Let $\mathbb G(\Gamma)$ and $\mathbb G(\Delta)$ be right-angled Artin groups, and let $\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)$ denote the core graph. **RAAG core classification conjecture.** If

$$
\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)\simeq\operatorname{Core}(\Delta),
$$

then $\mathbb G(\Gamma)\equiv\mathbb G(\Delta)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)$ is the RAAG with the smallest graph in its elementary class: if $\mathbb G(\Delta)\equiv\mathbb G(\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma))$, then $\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)<\Delta$. If $\mathbb G(\Gamma)\equiv\mathbb G(\Delta)$, then $\Delta$ is obtained from $\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)$ by adding redundant vertices. This would classify elementary equivalence of RAAGs by their cores; the first concrete consequence about non-abelian free groups is known by work of Sela and Kharlampovich–Miasnikov.

351162.title: Equal-component failure-state conjecture for proportional edge connectivity
351162.statement:
Let $G(n,m)$ denote the class of graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. For $r=\frac{1}{k}$, let $n$ be a multiple of $k$, and let $CO^{1/k}_{e}(G)$ and $CO^{1/k^+}_{e}(G(n,m))$ denote the proportional edge connectivity of a graph and the maximum such value over $G(n,m)$, respectively. A **failure state** is the graph obtained after removing an edge disconnecting set.

**Equal-component failure-state conjecture.** There exists $G\in G(n,m)$ such that

$$
CO^{1/k}_{e}(G)=CO^{1/k^+}_{e}(G(n,m))
$$

and the failure state of $G$ can be written as the union of $k$ components of order $\frac{n}{k}$.

The conjecture is intended to describe the structure of an extremal failure state and is used to seek upper bounds through bipartite subgraphs of graph complements. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.

351536.title: The degree-four planar line-graph conjecture
351536.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $L(G)$ denote its line graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. A graph is **word-representable** if it admits a word representation, and an orientation is **$k$-semi-transitive** when it satisfies the corresponding $k$-semi-transitivity condition. **Degree-four line-graph conjecture.** The line graph $L(G)$ of a graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\leq 4$ is at least 3-semi-transitively orientable. Moreover, if $G$ is non-word-representable, $\Delta(G)\leq 4$, and $G$ is planar, then $L(G)$ is word-representable.

The claim proposes relationships between the semi-transitivity and word-representability of a graph and those of its line graph, in the degree-four planar setting. The source presents these as possible relationships rather than established results; their general validity is not resolved there.

351888.title: The three-color conjecture for S-edge-colorings
351888.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}^{(k)}$ be the class of graphs specified in the paper, and let $\chi'_{\mathcal{S}}(G)$ denote the minimum number of colors in an edge-coloring of $G$ whose color classes belong to $\mathcal{S}$. A **Shannon triangle of type $(2,2,1)$** is a Shannon triangle whose three bouquets have even, even and odd cardinalities, respectively; its multiplicity is the parameter used in the paper to describe the repeated bouquet sizes.

**Three-color conjecture for $\mathcal{S}$-edge-colorings.** If $G$ is a connected loopless graph that is not a Shannon triangle of type $(2,2,1)$ with multiplicity at least $3$, then

$$
\chi'_{\mathcal{S}}(G)\leq3.
$$

The claim is motivated by examples showing that Shannon triangles of type $(2,2,1)$ and multiplicity at least $3$ require four colors for an $\mathcal{S}$-edge-coloring. The source presents the assertion as a tempting conjecture, without reporting a resolution.

352460.title: Strict increase of maximal embedding dimensions with base set size
352460.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and for a code $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ write $\operatorname{odim}(\mathcal C)$, $\operatorname{cdim}(\mathcal C)$, and $\operatorname{ndim}(\mathcal C)$ for its open, closed, and non-degenerate embedding dimensions. For each $n$, consider the maximum finite embedding dimension attained among codes on $[n]$. **Strict-increase conjecture.** The maximum open embedding dimension is a strictly increasing function of $n$: if $\mathcal C\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ and $\mathcal D\subseteq 2^{[n+1]}$ attain the respective maxima, then

$$
\operatorname{odim}(\mathcal D)>\operatorname{odim}(\mathcal C).
$$

The analogous strict increase should hold for closed and non-degenerate embedding dimensions. This would describe how efficiently neural codes on larger base sets can realize high-dimensional structures; the paper does not establish the conjecture, and the corresponding maxima remain a subject for further study.

352733.title: Spectral classification conjecture for hyperbolic orbifolds
352733.statement:
Let $E\subset \mathbb{R}$ be the set of values $\ell_1(X)$ as $X$ runs over all hyperbolic orbifolds. Let $\ell_1^{(0)}\approx15.79023$ be the smallest real number such that $E\cap(\ell_1^{(0)},+\infty)$ is discrete.

**Spectral classification conjecture.** The set $E$ is bounded above by $44.8883537$. The only orbifolds with $\ell_1>\ell_1^{(0)}$ are isometric to $[0;2,3,7]$, $[0;2,4,5]$, $[0;3,3,4]$, or $[0;2,3,8]$. The only orbifolds with $\ell_1=\ell_1^{(0)}$ are isometric to $[0;2,3,9]$ or the $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric point in the moduli space of $[0;2,2,2,3]$ orbifolds. Moreover, $E$ contains a non-empty open interval $(\ell_1^{(1)},\ell_1^{(0)})$ containing the values $\ell_1(X)$ for other points in that moduli space.

The conjecture proposes a global classification of the largest spectral values of hyperbolic orbifolds. The numerical equalities in the statement are non-rigorous estimates, while the preceding theorem supplies partial rigorous restrictions above a lower threshold.

353896.title: The forest-path partition conjecture for planar graphs without 4-cycles and 6-cycles
353896.statement:
Let a planar graph be a graph that can be embedded in the plane, and let a graph be **forest** if it is acyclic. A graph is a **linear forest** if each of its connected components is a path; write $\mathcal{F}_1$ for the class of forests whose maximum degree is at most $1$, and $\mathcal{F}$ for the class of all forests. An $(\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F})$-partition is a partition of the vertex set into two parts inducing, respectively, a graph in $\mathcal{F}_1$ and a graph in $\mathcal{F}$.

**Forest-path partition conjecture.** Every planar graph without $4$-cycles and $6$-cycles has an $(\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F})$-partition.

This conjecture seeks to strengthen known vertex-partition results for planar graphs excluding 4-cycles and 6-cycles: such graphs are known to admit both a $(\Delta_2,\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I})$-partition and an $(\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{I},\mathcal{I})$-partition, while the conjectured partition replaces the two independent-set parts with a single forest and retains a bounded-degree forest part. The source presents this as an open problem.

354915.title: Curran's standard bicentrally balanced labeling conjecture for projective grid graphs
354915.statement:
Let $m\geqslant 3$ and $n\geqslant 3$ be odd integers. Let $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$ be the $m\times n$ projective grid graph. A **standard bicentrally balanced** $C_4$-face-magic labeling is a labeling of the type specified in the paper, and an $(m,n)$-projective factorization sequence is the combinatorial datum used there to construct such labelings. Write $\operatorname{HBBL}(F)$ and $\operatorname{VBBL}(F')$ for the corresponding horizontal and vertical constructions.

**Curran's standard bicentrally balanced labeling conjecture.** If $X$ is a standard bicentrally balanced $C_4$-face-magic projective labeling on $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, then either there exists an $(m,n)$-projective factorization sequence $F$ such that $X=\operatorname{HBBL}(F)$, or there exists an $(n,m)$-projective factorization sequence $F'$ such that $X=\operatorname{VBBL}(F')$.

This conjecture asks whether the stated horizontal and vertical constructions exhaust all standard bicentrally balanced labelings. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.

355026.title: The degree-dependent partial-isolation bound conjecture
355026.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. For a positive integer $k$, let $\iota_k(G)$ denote the minimum size of a vertex set whose closed neighborhood leaves no induced copy of $K_k$, and let $ir(G)$ denote the irredundance number. Let $c_{\Delta}(k)$ be the corresponding least upper bound of $\iota_k(G)/ir(G)$ over graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. **The degree-dependent partial-isolation bound conjecture.** For $1\leq k\leq \Delta$,

$$
\iota_k(G)\leq c_{\Delta}(k)ir(G),
$$

where $c_{\Delta}(1),c_{\Delta}(2),\ldots,c_{\Delta}(\Delta)$ is a strictly decreasing sequence satisfying

$$
1\leq c_{\Delta}(k)<2.
$$

The conjecture proposes a degree-dependent hierarchy of bounds interpolating between partial isolation and irredundance. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so its status remains open.

355038.title: Characterization of extremal nonnegative tensors by unfolded permutation tensors
355038.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ denote the lower bound in equation (main) for the ratio of the spectral norm to the Frobenius norm. An **unfolded permutation tensor** is a tensor obtained by unfolding a permutation matrix, as defined in the surrounding discussion; multiplication by a positive constant means replacing $\mathcal{T}$ by $c\mathcal{T}$ for some $c>0$. **Characterization conjecture.** The lower bound $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is achieved by a nonnegative tensor if and only if that tensor is an unfolded permutation tensor up to multiplication by a positive constant. This would give a complete characterization of the tensors attaining the extreme spectral-to-Frobenius norm ratio; the paper states that this remains unresolved and develops a reduction to the case of maximum foldings with prime mode dimensions.

355948.title: Hafner's reverse-order recursive leading-monomial conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
355948.statement:
Fix $w\in S_n$ and any term order with $x_1>x_2>\cdots>x_n$. Let $\mathfrak{G}_w^{(k)}$ denote the degree-$k$ homogeneous component of $\mathfrak{G}_w$, and let $m_k(\bm{x})$ be its leading monomial. Let $C^S(w)$ be the staircase climbing chain with marked-link data $M(C^S(w))$, and write $\operatorname{wt}(C^S(w),M(C^S(w)))$ for its weight. **Hafner's reverse-order conjecture.** For $\ell(w)<k\leq \mathrm{raj}(w)$, 
$$
m_k(\bm{x})=x_p m_{k-1}(\bm{x}),
$$
 where $p$ is the smallest index such that $x_p m_{k-1}(\bm{x})$ divides $\bm{x}^{\operatorname{wt}(C^S(w),M(C^S(w)))}$. The conjecture predicts the leading monomials of the homogeneous components in the reverse variable order, using the staircase chain; it is presented as an analogue of the preceding conjecture and remains open in the supplied source.

356829.title: NP-completeness of minimal rook domination on convex polyominoes
356829.statement:
A **polyomino** is a finite union of edge-connected unit squares in the plane. It is **row-convex** if each row has at most one connected component, **column-convex** if each column has at most one connected component, and **convex** if it is both row-convex and column-convex. The minimal domination problem asks for the smallest attacking or non-attacking rook set that dominates the polyomino.

**Convex-polyomino rook domination conjecture.** The minimal domination problem for attacking or non-attacking rooks on convex polyominoes is NP-complete.

Minimal rook domination is trivial on square polyominoes but NP-complete on general polyominoes. The cited result of Alpert implies that proving the attacking-rook case is equivalent to proving the non-attacking case; the conjecture remains open.

360653.title: The GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture for exact slow NIM
360653.statement: Consider the exact slow game NIM$(n,n-1)$ for $\ell$ players: a position is a non-negative $n$-vector, players move cyclically, and on each move a player keeps one entry unchanged and decreases each of the other $n-1$ positive entries by $1$. A position with at least two non-positive entries is terminal; the player whose turn it is loses, and the other $\ell-1$ players share the payoff $\frac{C-L(P)}{\ell-1}$, where $L(P)$ is the play length and $C$ exceeds the length of every play from the initial position. The GM-rule specifies a strategy for each player, including the move that keeps the largest entry when no entry is a multiple of $\ell$. **GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture.** The set of $\ell$ GM-strategies forms a uniform Nash equilibrium. The claim concerns the strategic behavior induced by the GM-rule in the multiplayer exact slow NIM game; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

361128.title: Nash equilibrium conjecture for the GM-strategies in exact slow NIM
361128.statement: Let $x$ be a position in the exact slow game $\operatorname{NIM}(n,n-1)$ played by $\ell$ players in a fixed cyclic order. A move reduces $n-1$ positive entries by $1$ and leaves one entry unchanged; terminal positions have at least two non-positive entries. The GM-rule assigns a strategy to each player, including the rule that when no entry of $x$ is a multiple of $\ell$, the largest entry is kept unchanged and the other $n-1$ entries are reduced by $1$. **Nash equilibrium conjecture.** The set of $\ell$ GM-strategies form a uniform Nash equilibrium. The claim concerns the strategic behavior of the exact slow NIM game with multiple players and asserts that the GM-strategies are jointly stable under unilateral deviation. The supplied text does not state whether this has been proved or remains open.

381721.title: The prime-cycle clique extremal conjecture
381721.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $\mathcal C_{\geq p}^{\mathrm{prime}}$ be the family of all cycles of length at least $p$. For integers $n$ and $r$ satisfying $r<p$, let $ex(n,K_r,\mathcal C_{\geq p}^{\mathrm{prime}})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $K_r$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no member of $\mathcal C_{\geq p}^{\mathrm{prime}}$. **Prime-cycle clique extremal conjecture.**

$$
ex(n,K_r,\mathcal C_{\geq p}^{\mathrm{prime}})\leq \frac{n-1}{p-2}\binom{p-1}{r}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $n-1$ is divisible by $p-2$ and the extremal graph is a connected $n$-vertex graph consisting of $\frac{n-1}{p-2}$ maximal $2$-connected blocks, each isomorphic to $K_{p-1}$. This proposes a prime-parameter analogue of the preceding clique bound for graphs with forbidden long cycles; no resolution is supplied in the source.

404028.title: Ascending subgraph decomposition conjecture
404028.statement:
Every graph $G$ with $\binom{m}{2}$ edges has an edge decomposition into subgraphs $H_1,\ldots,H_{m-1}$ such that $e(H_i)=i$ and, for each $1\le i\le m-2$, $H_i$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $H_{i+1}$.

Such a decomposition is called an ascending subgraph decomposition.
